resources.string:
Black Sigatoka, also known as black leaf streak disease, is one of the most serious fungal diseases affecting banana plants.

It is caused by the fungus Mycosphaerella fijiensis.

This disease attacks the leaves of the banana plant, reducing its ability to perform photosynthesis properly.

As the infection becomes severe, banana production decreases, fruits become smaller, and the overall quality of the harvest is affected.

Black Sigatoka spreads quickly in warm and humid environments, especially during long periods of rainfall.

Panama Disease, also known as Fusarium wilt, is a highly destructive fungal disease caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense.

The fungus attacks the vascular system of the banana plant, blocking the movement of water and nutrients from the roots to the leaves.

This disease is considered one of the most dangerous threats to banana production worldwide because the fungus can survive in the soil for many years.

Once a plantation becomes infected, the disease is very difficult to eliminate completely.

Cordana Leaf Spot is a fungal disease of banana plants caused by Cordana musae.

Although it is generally less destructive than Black Sigatoka, it can still weaken banana plants when left unmanaged.

The disease mainly affects older leaves and is more common in areas with high humidity and poor air circulation.

Continuous infection may reduce photosynthetic activity and affect plant growth and fruit production.
